newsitem.title: USA: Waban and Kmart divisons call off merger.
newsitem.headline: Waban and Kmart divisons call off merger.

text.p: Waban Inc. said Wednesday it has ended discussions to merge its HomeBase home improvement retailing division with the Builders Square division of Kmart Corp.

The merger would have produced one of the nation's largest home improvement companies, with about 250 stores in 25 states and annual revenues of nearly $4 billion. The talks were announced in early February.

Waban said discussions with Kmart and Leonard Green & Partners LP had not produced an agreement acceptable to all parties. The Natick, Mass.-based company said it will proceed with its previously announced plan to spin off its BJ's Wholesdale Club division in a special dividend to Waban shareholders.
BJ's Wholesale Club is one of the largest membership warehouse club chains in the northeastern United States, with 81 outlets.

Waban said it expects to file a registration statement within two weeks with the Securities and Exchange Commission regarding the proposed spin-off in July. It expects to hold a shareholders' meeting in June to seek approval for the transaction.
HomeBase operates 84 home improvement stores in the western United States.
Waban's stock fell 62.5 cents to $27.25, while Kmart slipped 12.5 cents to $11.875 on the New York Stock Exchange.
